parts.why: The raw low-outcome insula responses (Social > Partner) are one measure of the insula ROI guilt result, which subtracts the high-outcome response from this.
The low-minus-high difference being larger in Social is the 'even after subtracting high outcomes' clause of the insula ROI guilt result stated on its own.
The R-squared comparison across models is one leg of the model-selection verdict that the Responsibility model fitted the happiness data best.
That happiness varied with the participant's own rewards is one component of the reward dependencies the Responsibility Redux model was fitted to capture.
That happiness varied with the partner's rewards is the other reward-source component the Responsibility Redux model captures.
The frequency of risky choice across Solo and Social is one of the three measures the 'similar risk preferences' conclusion integrates.
The risk-aversion parameter rho comparison is the second risk measure the 'similar risk preferences' conclusion integrates.
The risk-premium comparison is the third measure feeding the 'similar risk preferences' conclusion, reconciled with the small Study 1 rho tendency.
That the guilt effect held whether the participant's own outcome was high or low is one robustness condition of the behavioural guilt effect.
The null for high partner outcomes states the boundary condition that the guilt effect is specific to low outcomes.
